_README: Edge-Function deploy ledger (B-178 / CUL-135). One entry per deployable function. `fingerprint` = the sha256 of the function's shipping import-closure (index.ts + every local .ts it inlines) last acknowledged for deploy — computed by guards/edgeFunctionDeploy.test.ts, which FAILS THE BUILD when a function drifts from its recorded fingerprint without a reasoned acknowledgment. Statuses: `deployed` (fingerprint confirmed live), `pending` (a deploy is owed OR the live state is unverified — see the entry's `reason`), `hold` (deliberately not deployed — e.g. B-494). `pending`/`hold` require a `reason`. After deploying a function, set its `fingerprint` to the current value (the guard's failure message prints it) with status `deployed`. This ledger records intent; it does NOT prove a deploy happened — see docs/edge-deploy-runbook.md § Deploy ledger.

RE-FINGERPRINTED 2026-09-16 for R-14 (CUL-291), merged on top of R-16: the trend chart now marks intervention STOPS as well as starts. No response-shape change, no new pull, no scope change — it is render plus one additive field on an internal structure. The HTML DIFFERS from R-16's on any report whose window contains an owner-declared end.

WHAT IS OWED — R-14 (CUL-291), the stops. The chart drew a dashed vertical where a diet, medication or supplement STARTED and nothing where one stopped, so the reading a clinician actually asks the chart for — a steroid coming off as the flares fell, which is the strongest argument the record holds for a diet working — was undrawable, while "Reading the trend" counted that same withdrawal as a change in prose. The chart and the sentence beside it disagreed. A stop is now its own glyph (a long-dashed rule with a heavy flat head; two non-colour channels, because §5.8's bar is a photocopy), the marker legend DRAWS both marks and names both, and ONE predicate (`isWindowChange`) is what the chart, the legend and the count all switch on. A food added to a trial's allowed list mid-trial is a diet change by the legend's own definition and now draws — on the clean fixture a treat permitted Jun 8 and fed 25 times had no marker and a count that said two changes; it says three.

TWO THINGS THE REVIEW PASSES FORCED, both of which change what a DEPLOYED report says, so they matter to whoever reads the artifact after this lands:

  • A STOP IS ONLY DRAWN FOR AN OWNER-DECLARED END. An ad-hoc course (doses with no regimen row) has its span derived from the record, ending at `lastDate` — the last dose LOGGED. An owner who keeps giving a drug and stops logging it produces exactly the value an owner who stopped it produces. The first cut drew `med stop` over that, contradicting §4.4's lifetime table on the same page, over the same dose rows, under a caption that says a course with no end date is one whose end the owner never recorded, "not one still under way". `ConcurrentChange.endIsDeclared` now records whether the SOURCE COLUMN is an owner action, the glyph is gated on it, and the prose reads "last dose logged <date>" rather than "stopped <date>" where it is false. So a deployed report will say "last dose logged" for ad-hoc courses where it previously said "stopped" — that is the fix, not a regression.

  • MARKERS PAINT AFTER THE BARS AND INVERT TO WHITE OVER THEM. They were emitted first and the bar fill is near-black, so every rule crossing a column was painted out; on a bar at the axis maximum only ~3px survived, which is exactly the week an intervention starts in. Nothing else about the bars changed.

Also: a permission is never spoken as an exposure (the face reads `permitted`, the note "(permitted from Jun 8)", never "started" — saying "started" over a permission row manufactures a food challenge with a negative result over zero feedings); marker labels are LAID OUT rather than placed, after two marks three days apart overprinted into an unreadable string on the clean fixture; and a drawn stop earns one caveat, "One of them ending inside this window does not make the rest of it a single-agent period", because the marker carves out an apparently de-confounded stretch and the caution's own rationale otherwise tells a sharp reader the prohibition lapses there.

AFTER DEPLOYING, for R-14 specifically: regenerate the affected pet's report and confirm (e) the trend chart carries a flat-headed vertical at each owner-declared end (cetirizine stopped Sep 5 was the v15 cold-read case), that the marker legend above the charts draws both glyphs and reads "started … one stopped", and that no ad-hoc course carries a stop glyph or the word "stopped". Then re-run `vet-report-cold-read` on the fresh artifact.
